newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares up on year-end window dressing.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares up on year-end window dressing.

text.p: Late session window-dressing pushed Jakarta share prices higher at the close of the last trading day of the year, brokers said.
"In order to record a better performance at the end of the year, many companies are doing window-dressing," a local broker said.
She said the rise in the index appeared to be planned, as investors had shown limited interest in morning trade but some counters made significant gains towards the close.
The composite index rose 4.94 points, or 0.78 percent, to close at 637.43 points after touching a low of 632.28 points.

Advancers led decliners by 76 to 36, with 68 counters unchanged. Total volume was 231.7 million shares, with turnover of 555.6 billion rupiah, boosted by sales of heavyweight Telkom in cross-trade on a volume of 43.1 million shares.
Brokers said a block sale of Astra International on a volume of five million shares also pushed up trading volume.
"For a few days, there has been speculation that Putera Sampoerna was selling its stake in Astra which we could not confirm," a local broker said.
Comment from Putera Sampoerna was not available.
Brokers said the market was likely to be sluggish on the first trading day in 1997, Thursday, January 2.
"Many investors will remain on holiday. I think the market will be back to normal by mid-January," an analyst with a Japanese securities firm said.

Agribusiness firm Sierad Produce topped the active list on its debut on Friday with a turnover of 30.9 million shares. But it eased to 825 rupiah after rising 75 rupiah from its offer price of 900 rupiah per share.
"It is very disappointing. This is bad timing for a listing date," a local broker said.
Brokers attributed the poor performance to overall weak sentiment due to the holiday season.
They also said rioting in the West Javan town of Tasikmalaya on Thursday put some pressure on market sentiment.
"But the impact appeared to be limited because many players have been sidelined due to the holiday season," a broker said.
Great River, Medco Energy and Dharmala Sakti were among the gainers due to window-dressing, brokers said.
Great River rose 175 rupiah to 1,600 on 4.6 million shares after touching a low of 1,325 rupiah at mid-session.
Oil and natural gas explorer Medco Energy rose 225 rupiah to 4,300 on a turnover of 2.5 million shares after dipping to 4,000 rupiah.

Information technology and retail firm Multipolar and retailer Matahari were active, making gains on fresh buying after a recent announcement that Multipolar will pay 673 billion rupiah in cash and notes for a 45 percent stake in retailer Matahari.
Multipolar, part of the diversified Lippo Group, has initiated a tender offer to buy a further 5.1 percent stake in Matahari.
Multipolar rose 50 rupiah to 1,600 on a volume of about 7.3 million shares, while Matahari rose 50 rupiah to 2,750 on 4.5 million shares.
Brokers said analysts were re-evaluating the two companies following the announcement.
"I recommend long-term buy for both companies. From the information they give, this alliance will boost their revenue," an analyst with a Japanese-firm said.
